about: Trees of U1c, as every renderer shows them. A tree's rows are the records of a list in the window (`rows`, each with its `id` and the id of its `parent`, or null), arranged by that parent: a row whose parent is in the list shows under it, any other row at the top. Rows keep the order of the list, under their parent as at the top. A loop of parents is broken at the row of the loop that comes first in the list, which shows at the top. `open` names the ids of the rows shown open; a closed row hides what is under it. `shows` is the rows shown, top to bottom, each as [its place in the list counted from 0, its depth from 0, whether rows are under it]. `reveal` opens every row above the row at place `at`, as a tree does when that row is selected; `opens` is the ids opened, in the order of the list.

cases.name: an open row shows the rows under it, in the order of the list
an open row under a closed one stays hidden
a row whose parent is not in the list shows at the top
a child may come before its parent in the list
a loop of parents is broken at its first row
a row that is its own parent
